preconditions.description: The number of cities (nodes) in the tree is between 5 and 200,000 inclusive.
Each of the n-1 road descriptions contains exactly two distinct integers representing connected cities.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:n] for x in line.split())
preconditions.description: All city identifiers in road descriptions are valid integers between 1 and n inclusive.
The number of test cases is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.
Each test case line contains exactly four integers representing u, v, x, y.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[n+1:] for x in line.split())
preconditions.description: All city identifiers in test cases are valid integers between 1 and n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(int(u) != int(v) and int(x) != int(y) for line in stdin.splitlines()[n+1:] for u, v, x, y in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: In each test case, u ≠ v and x ≠ y.

postconditions.description: Each output line contains exactly one integer or -1.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line in ['0', '-1'] or (int(stdout_line) >= 0 and int(stdout_line) <= 2 * 10**5) for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output is either 0 (meet at start), -1 (never meet), or a non-negative integer representing the meeting time in minutes.

postconditions.expression: all((int(stdout_line) == 0) == (u == x and v == y) for (u, v, x, y), stdout_line in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[n+1:]], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: If the starting cities and paths of both runners are identical (u == x and v == y), the output is 0.

postconditions.expression: all((int(stdout_line) == -1) == (not any((u == x and v == y) or (u == y and v == x) or (x == u and y == v) or (x == v and y == u)) and not any((int(stdout_line) >= 0) and (int(stdout_line) <= 2 * 10**5))) for (u, v, x, y), stdout_line in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[n+1:]], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: If the runners' paths are disjoint (no common city in their paths) and no meeting time is found, the output is -1.

postconditions.expression: all((int(stdout_line) >= 0) == any((u == x and v == y) or (u == y and v == x) or (x == u and y == v) or (x == v and y == u)) for (u, v, x, y), stdout_line in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[n+1:]], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: If the runners' paths share at least one city, the output is a non-negative integer representing the first meeting time.

postconditions.expression: all((int(stdout_line) == 0) or (int(stdout_line) == -1) or (int(stdout_line) == min_time) for (u, v, x, y), stdout_line in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[n+1:]], stdout.splitlines()) if (min_time := find_min_meeting_time(u, v, x, y, tree)) is not None)
postconditions.description: If a meeting time exists, the output is the smallest non-negative integer representing the first time both runners are at the same city. The function `find_min_meeting_time` is defined as the smallest time t >= 0 where the positions of both runners coincide.
